baseline.description: Versioned behavior baseline for replacing the wxPython UI with the modern React UI without reducing PixelFlasher safety or functionality.
baseline.dynamicItemPolicy: Server/version generated firmware entries, user-defined My Tools entries, and connected-device entries are represented by their generating handler contract rather than by one row per runtime value.

capabilities.capability: Dashboard and device summary
capabilities.exitContract: Dashboard state, warnings and recommended next action are driven by the modern state store.

capabilities.capability: Guided stock/custom-ROM flash workspace
capabilities.exitContract: Every flash option and preflight state is reachable and reviewable without the legacy frame.

capabilities.capability: Device state workspace
capabilities.exitContract: Device identity, connection mode, slot and root state have native modern presentation.

capabilities.capability: Backup workspace
capabilities.exitContract: The React workspace and backend-safe create/restore service exist, but the UI still needs native path, partition and slot inputs plus a canonical refreshed inventory; list/import/delete parity remains open.

capabilities.capability: Firmware download workspace
capabilities.exitContract: Available builds, download integrity and selection are native modern state.

capabilities.capability: Settings workspace
capabilities.exitContract: Theme, locale, contrast, reduced motion and zoom are loaded and updated by the real React host through strict atomic settings.get/settings.update contracts; the workspace remains partial because the broader 9.x application settings and expert-mode preference are not covered. Mock preview isolation still uses local storage by design.

capabilities.capability: Tool catalog workspace
capabilities.exitContract: The React workspace reaches managed scrcpy, secret-safe wireless ADB, a bounded logcat viewer, native file push, partition list/read/write/erase and atomic support export. Advanced utilities plus the per-capability packaging, progress, postcondition and legacy-data gaps remain open.

capabilities.capability: Safety policy and confirmation workspace
capabilities.exitContract: SafetyPolicy emits revision-bound interaction requests through the runtime broker; the accessible React modal returns accepted or cancelled over the single bridge before the engine revalidates the immutable plan.

capabilities.capability: Version, licensing and project information
capabilities.exitContract: Version, license, update and support information matches the packaged application.

capabilities.capability: Scan, select and disambiguate multiple devices
capabilities.exitContract: Headless adb/fastboot scanning returns typed, serial-keyed devices with cancellation and partial-source preservation. Fastboot enrichment reads only serial-bound current-slot, unlocked and is-userspace getvars, distinguishes fastbootd, and merges prior identity metadata without treating stale root, slot or bootloader state as fresh evidence; selection rejects serials absent from the latest inventory and remains stable across refreshes.

capabilities.capability: Locate, validate or install Android Platform Tools
capabilities.exitContract: Local path/PATH discovery natively validates a co-located executable adb/fastboot pair, equal parseable versions at or above the minimum, cancellation and typed failures; parity still requires checksum-verified atomic download/install, which currently returns network_setup_not_supported.

capabilities.capability: Select and identify a factory or full OTA package
capabilities.exitContract: The packaged React flow uses a native file picker and firmware.select; inspection canonicalizes the path, streams SHA-256, classifies factory/OTA/custom archives, rejects corruption, traversal and selected-device mismatch, and supports cancellation. Full parity still requires the official catalog/download-to-selection flow and complete user-facing diagnostics.

capabilities.capability: Select a custom ROM archive
capabilities.exitContract: The native picker and classifier accept custom direct-image archives and apply device compatibility checks before processing. A dedicated custom-ROM experience, payload.bin processing and the complete stock/custom substitution diagnostics remain open.

capabilities.capability: Validate and process factory/full OTA packages
capabilities.exitContract: firmware.process accepts no browser-supplied paths, hashes, argv or staging locations. It performs bounded fail-closed factory extraction or verified OTA registration, builds typed hash-bound planner inventory, promotes firmware and stock boot atomically, and rehydrates only verified cached artifacts. Complete product diagnostics, retry UX and packaged cross-platform validation remain open.

capabilities.capability: Process custom ROM packages
capabilities.exitContract: Direct-image custom ROM archives are validated, compatibility-checked, extracted to fixed backend paths, hashed and registered as typed planner artifacts without a legacy handler; a verified boot/init_boot image is required before atomic promotion. Custom payload.bin processing is explicitly unsupported and remains the principal parity gap.

capabilities.capability: Browse and download phone/watch factory, OTA, beta and canary images
capabilities.exitContract: Native downloads preserve published SHA-256 metadata, progress, cancellation and final package selection.

capabilities.capability: Factory flash while keeping user data
capabilities.exitContract: The React option is compiled by the backend into an immutable plan that omits -w, using the native service's verified, hash-bound factory or direct-image artifact inventory. Full parity still requires remaining runtime transition, mode and multi-device coverage.

capabilities.capability: Factory flash with explicit data wipe
capabilities.exitContract: Selecting wipe, reviewing exact argv and executing are separate backend-guarded decisions bound to revision, serial, plan fingerprint and firmware/artifact hashes. Verified factory artifacts are now produced and registered natively; complete transition orchestration, device-state recovery and packaged hardware coverage remain open.

capabilities.capability: Generate and inspect a flash plan without device writes
capabilities.exitContract: Dry-run is serialized into the canonical fingerprint and the executor launches zero subprocesses. Factory and direct-image custom plans now consume the same backend-produced artifact inventory as real execution; remaining parity gaps are the unsupported custom payload path and unimplemented transition/batch variants.

capabilities.capability: Full OTA sideload to inactive slot
capabilities.exitContract: A verified processed OTA in sideload mode compiles to exact serial-bound adb sideload/reboot argv with incompatible options rejected explicitly; native recovery-to-sideload transition orchestration remains open.

capabilities.capability: Review and execute the complete flash plan
capabilities.exitContract: The browser updates canonical intent, previews backend-compiled exact argv and calls flash.execute without supplying an operation plan; the engine constructs the immutable plan, performs reinforced confirmation when required and revalidates revision, serial, device mode, plan fingerprint and artifact hashes immediately before execution. Factory, OTA and direct-image custom inputs now reach the planner through verified registered artifacts. Full parity remains open for custom payload processing, recovery/fastbootd transition orchestration, multi-device batch execution and complete packaged-platform validation.

capabilities.capability: Patch boot/init_boot/vendor_boot with supported rooting applications
capabilities.exitContract: The typed React/bridge/backend flow supports Magisk, APatch, KernelSU, KernelSU-Next, SukiSU, Wild_KSU and Legacy, accepts only an opaque verified app ID plus flavor and destination, and compiles serial-, revision-, source-, APK- and runner-hash-bound plans. PatchResourceRegistry rejects unpinned, unconstrained or incompatible resources. PixelFlasher currently packages no real provider APKs or compatible runners, so execution fails closed; APatch secret transport and KMI/architecture-based kernel selection also remain open.

capabilities.capability: Flash the selected boot/init_boot/vendor_boot image
capabilities.exitContract: The React control requires one unlocked fastboot device and a verified canonical image; the backend compiles and revalidates exact partition, slot, image hash and serial without accepting argv. A post-command scan that proves the resulting partition/slot/device state is still missing.

capabilities.capability: Create a sanitized support package
capabilities.exitContract: The native host exchanges the chosen path for a one-use opaque grant; the core applies mandatory redaction, verifies an atomic ZIP and manifests included/omitted sources. The legacy database, recursive file listing and encrypted wrapper remain intentionally omitted until safely migrated.

capabilities.capability: List, create, import and delete Magisk boot backups
capabilities.exitContract: Backend-native bounded boot-chain create and restore use canonical paths, explicit slots, verified artifacts, typed failures and confirmation for restore. React now supplies native-picker paths plus partition and slot; persisted inventory/result presentation and Magisk list/import/delete contracts remain open.

capabilities.capability: Edit PixelFlasher application settings
capabilities.exitContract: The real React form and runtime load, merge and atomically persist theme, locale, high contrast, reduced motion and zoom through settings.get/settings.update with revision checks. Expert Mode now controls advanced disclosure, but host persistence for it and the remaining supported 9.x settings are open.

capabilities.capability: Download/install Magisk, KernelSU variants, APatch, SukiSU and Wild_KSU
capabilities.exitContract: The backend inventories canonical rooting APKs with provenance and hashes and installs only opaque backend-issued IDs. React inventory/install, verified download and channel/version selection remain open.

capabilities.capability: Manage Magisk-compatible modules and root settings
capabilities.exitContract: Backend-native list, enable, disable, validated-ZIP install and remove return typed state with action-specific confirmations. The complete React manager and update workflow remain open.

capabilities.capability: List, dump and erase one or more partitions
capabilities.exitContract: React exposes partition list/results plus native-picker read/write and guarded erase. The backend enforces a closed vocabulary, one current fastboot serial, canonical paths and exact argv; write requires confirmation and erase is reinforced. Device-side post-write/erase verification and richer progress/retry remain open.

capabilities.capability: Reboot to system, bootloader, fastbootd, recovery, safe mode, download or sideload
capabilities.exitContract: System, recovery, bootloader and fastbootd are compiled to serial-bound argv with state validation and typed process results; safe mode, download and sideload destinations plus post-transition verification remain open.

capabilities.capability: Standalone wipe shortcut
capabilities.exitContract: No standalone wipe bypass exists; any supported wipe is part of a fully reviewed immutable plan.

capabilities.capability: Change the active slot
capabilities.exitContract: The React flow submits an explicit target slot and the backend binds a reinforced challenge to serial, revision and plan before exact fastboot execution; a post-command scan that verifies the resulting active slot is still missing.

capabilities.capability: Wireless ADB discovery, pairing and connection
capabilities.exitContract: React exposes status, pair, connect and disconnect for validated numeric endpoints; the pairing code crosses a secret-stdin boundary and verified responses never echo it. Wireless discovery/mDNS, operation without an already selected ADB device and robust post-scan handoff remain open.

capabilities.capability: Install APK with ownership and low-target-SDK options
capabilities.exitContract: The backend validates and hashes one canonical APK and compiles allow-listed install flags with shell-free serial-bound argv and confirmation; no React APK picker/options flow emits this intent yet.

capabilities.capability: Package listing, filtering, enable/disable, uninstall, download, launch, permissions, clear/kill, denylist and SU controls
capabilities.exitContract: The backend natively lists scopes and compiles enable, disable, uninstall, clear-data, force-stop, launch, permissions and install intents with typed targets and confirmation metadata. React invokes apps.list for canonical refresh and exposes enable/disable; download, denylist, SU controls and the remaining actions stay open.

capabilities.capability: Interactive ADB shell
capabilities.exitContract: The visible tool is intentionally rejected with adb_shell_unsupported and launches no process; parity requires a separate explicit expert-only contract if arbitrary shell access is retained.

capabilities.capability: Launch scrcpy for the selected device
capabilities.exitContract: The React action and managed launcher bind one selected ADB serial, validate a backend-owned executable artifact and report launch failure without shell execution. Runtime executable discovery/packaging, configurable options and cross-platform lifecycle smokes remain open.

capabilities.capability: Device info, props JSON, PIF print, screen XML, bootloader versions and open URL
capabilities.exitContract: Each report is native, cancellable, serial-bound and safely exportable.

capabilities.capability: Cancel Google OTA, inspect otacerts and monitor update_engine
capabilities.exitContract: Mutation and read-only diagnostics are separate typed flows with clear ownership and results.

capabilities.capability: Logcat viewer and filtered update_engine logs
capabilities.exitContract: The React workspace renders the shell-free, serial-bound, timeout/line-bounded line model in a bounded viewer. Streaming updates, cancellation while streaming, redaction, export and update_engine-specific views remain open.

capabilities.capability: Push files to /data/local/tmp or Downloads
capabilities.exitContract: React provides a native multi-file picker, closed destination selector and typed result. The backend restricts destinations to /data/local/tmp/ or Downloads, canonicalizes and hashes sources, confirms and revalidates; per-file progress/retry and device-side hash verification remain open.

capabilities.capability: List, add, delete and inspect boot-image records and provenance
capabilities.exitContract: Native store supports full metadata, import, delete and deterministic selection.

capabilities.capability: Temporarily live-boot a selected image
capabilities.exitContract: The React control requires one unlocked fastboot device and a verified canonical image; the backend revalidates image hash and serial before exact fastboot boot execution. Reconnect/boot-outcome observation and typed postcondition reporting remain open.

capabilities.capability: Both/inactive slots, verity/verification, force, no-reboot, downgrade and temporary-root options
capabilities.exitContract: The React wizard exposes slot, verity, verification, force, no-reboot, downgrade and temporary-root intent and the planner either serializes each option into exact argv or rejects it with option_not_supported_for_mode; downgrade artifact generation is still absent.

capabilities.capability: Lock and unlock the bootloader
capabilities.exitContract: Expert React controls reach exact serial-bound fastboot lock/unlock plans with reinforced confirmation and mandatory wipe metadata. Lock now fails closed unless revision-bound backend evidence proves a complete compatible stock factory flash across both slots; because no trusted evidence producer exists yet, the real host disables lock by default. Evidence production and post-operation bootloader-state verification remain open.

capabilities.capability: Backup, restore and clear /data/adb
capabilities.exitContract: Archive validation, exact target and clear/restore confirmations are enforced below the UI.

capabilities.capability: PIF/TargetedFix management and Play Integrity analysis
capabilities.exitContract: All documented PIF, keybox, target, checker and analysis operations are inventoried and independently testable.

capabilities.capability: Start Shizuku and SOS-disable root modules
capabilities.exitContract: Both flows are serial-bound, explicit about effects and verify the resulting service/module state.

capabilities.capability: Keybox validation, binary XML decode and AVB image/downgrade tools
capabilities.exitContract: Inputs, outputs and validation errors are available without wx dialogs.

capabilities.capability: Create, edit, delete and launch My Tools entries
capabilities.exitContract: User-defined commands remain an explicit advanced surface and are never confused with guarded built-in actions.

capabilities.capability: Enable/disable device scanning and manage connected devices
capabilities.exitContract: Scan policy and device toggles are editable and reflected by the native device store.

capabilities.capability: Toolbar layout, language selection, links, update checks, folders, about and exit
capabilities.exitContract: All application-shell commands are keyboard accessible and packaged locale JSON stays in parity with gettext.

capabilities.capability: Native open/save file and directory dialogs for the React UI
capabilities.exitContract: The host constrains picker options, returns JSON-only canonical paths and never accepts executable callbacks from web content.

riskDefinitions.host_read: Reads local files without modifying them.
riskDefinitions.host_write: Downloads, extracts, configures or writes host files.
riskDefinitions.device_read: Queries a connected Android device without intended mutation.
riskDefinitions.device_write: Changes device state but is not inherently a data-erasing operation.
riskDefinitions.destructive: Can erase data, write boot-critical partitions, remove applications/data or execute arbitrary user commands.

statusDefinitions.native: Implemented by modern state/use cases without opening or delegating to legacy UI handlers.
statusDefinitions.read_only: Modern UI renders current state but does not provide the complete native mutation flow.
statusDefinitions.delegated: Reachable from the modern UI but execution still calls a legacy handler/frame.
statusDefinitions.partial: Only a documented subset is present in the modern UI.
statusDefinitions.blocked: Shown as intentionally unavailable until its safe native contract exists.
statusDefinitions.missing: No equivalent modern control or flow exists.
